h1:
Where to Stay in Ayutthaya?
10 Stays We've Reviewed
Prices Compared Across 3 Sites
heroSub: Ten Ayutthaya stays across every budget — a red-brick riverside boutique on the Chao Phraya, wooden guesthouses in the old town within walking distance of the temples, kitchen-suite hotels on Rojana Road, down to a garden hostel from ฿400/night. Covering the three areas travellers actually use: the Old Town island, the riverside, and the train-station district.
introH2: 🏛️ Why does choosing the right area in Ayutthaya matter so much?
introHtml: Ayutthaya looks like a small town you can do in a day, but where you stay shapes the trip more than you'd think. The Old Town island is the heart of it — walk or cycle to Wat Mahathat, Wat Ratchaburana and the historical park, and catch the Buddha head in the tree roots at dawn before the tour groups arrive. The riverside (Chao Phraya and Pa Sak) is for quiet stays, some looking across the water to ancient stupas. Rojana Road on the city's edge suits self-drivers who want big rooms with a kitchen. Many travellers book without checking the area, then burn the day shuttling in and out of the historical park. This guide brings together 10 Ayutthaya stays we've actually read the reviews for and picked across every tier — prices compared across 3 sites with direct booking links throughout.
mrtHtml: Ayutthaya has no metro · from Bangkok you can come by train (alight at Ayutthaya station), minivan or self-drive · around town, cycling, tuk-tuks and Grab make it easy, and many stays lend or rent bicycles. The main areas in this guide: Old Town island — Tamarind, Baan Mee Suk, iuDia, Baan Tye Wang, Busaba, Plus Hostel, all within walking or cycling distance of the temples · Riverside — SALA Ayutthaya (Chao Phraya, facing Wat Phutthaisawan), Krungsri River (Pa Sak, near the train station) · Rojana Road — Classic Kameo, Kantary, kitchen-suite hotels on the city's edge near malls and markets.

entries.name: SALA Ayutthaya
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Chao Phraya riverside, Pratu Chai · facing Wat Phutthaisawan
entries.addr: 9/2 Moo 4, U-Thong Road, Pratu Chai, Ayutthaya
entries.storyHtml: SALA Ayutthaya is the 5-star riverside boutique where the architecture genuinely tells Ayutthaya's story, scoring 9.3 · Opened in 2014 and designed by Onion studio, it uses the same red brick used to restore the temples, set against smooth whitewashed walls · River-view rooms look straight across the Chao Phraya to the stupa of Wat Phutthaisawan · There's a riverside restaurant, freshly cooked à la carte breakfast, a rooftop bar, and a private courtyard pool.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Book a River View or River View Terrace room and ask for a higher floor — the view of the river and the stupa opposite is the real reason to stay here.
pros: Chao Phraya riverside, looking across to Wat Phutthaisawan's stupa
Striking red-brick-and-whitewash design that photographs beautifully
Warm service, soft beds, lovely riverside breakfast
Great base for cycling the historical park
cons: Limited storage in rooms and bathrooms
Only 27 rooms — fills fast on weekends, peak rates climb

entries.name: Plus Hostel Ayutthaya
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Thawasukree, Old Town island · cycle to the temples
entries.storyHtml: The highest score in this guide at 9.7 from 614 reviews — Plus Hostel is the garden house where owners Gong and Ja cook free dinner and breakfast every day, with everyone eating together at one table like family · The garden setting is calm, with hammocks, a fish pond and friendly pets · Dorm beds are new bunks with privacy curtains, lockers and reading lights · It earns the number-two spot on consistently high scores and review volume, even as a 2-star stay.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Stay in for the shared dinner at least one night — it's where you meet the owners and other travellers, and it's the real charm of the place.
pros: Owners are wonderfully kind, looking after guests like family
Free dinner and breakfast daily — the owner's pad thai gets a lot of mentions
Quiet garden setting with hammocks and pets
Clean rooms, beds with privacy curtains, from just ฿400
cons: Thawasukree area is about 1 km from the main temples — walk or cycle
Small hostel, shared dorms, no pool

entries.name: Classic Kameo Hotel & Serviced Apartments
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Rojana Road · business/mall district, city edge
entries.addr: 210-211, 148 Moo 5, Rojana Road, Phai Ling, Ayutthaya
entries.storyHtml: Classic Kameo is the 4-star hotel-plus-serviced-apartment with the most reviews in this guide — 403 of them, scoring 9.2 · The draw is spacious, clean rooms; Studio and One Bedroom Suites add a kitchenette and seating area, ideal for families and longer stays · The buffet breakfast gets repeated praise, and there's a pool, gym, sauna and generous free parking · The trade-off is the Rojana Road location on the city's edge — you drive into the historical park.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: If you're a group or staying several nights, pick a Studio or One Bedroom Suite with a kitchen — far better value than a Deluxe — and ask for a room away from Rojana Road for quiet.
pros: Very spacious, clean rooms; many with a kitchenette and seating
Varied buffet breakfast, widely praised
Pool, gym, sauna and free parking
Great value, especially for groups or longer stays
cons: City-edge Rojana Road location — can't walk to the ruins
Some AC units are older; roadside rooms catch traffic noise

entries.name: Baan Tye Wang Guesthouse
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Pratu Chai, Old Town island · near the historical park
tags: 🏡 Thai house in a garden with pond
entries.addr: 223/18 Moo 8, Pratu Chai, Old Town island, Ayutthaya
entries.storyHtml: Baan Tye Wang is the boutique Thai-house guesthouse run personally by its owners, scoring 9.3 from 133 reviews and 4.8 on TripAdvisor (ranked #2 among Ayutthaya guesthouses) · It's a small wooden house in a green garden with a pond, in the middle of the Old Town island · What guests mention most is the hospitable owner family who welcome and help you themselves, leaving many feeling like they're staying with relatives · There's an outdoor rain shower, fresh breakfast served in the garden, and free bicycles.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: If insects bother you, ask for a room away from the pond and bring repellent · Borrow the bikes to cycle the historical park in the early morning or evening for the easiest, prettiest ride.
pros: Hospitable owner family who look after guests personally
Quiet Thai-garden setting with a shady pond
Tasty fresh breakfast that changes daily
Free bikes, free parking, good value
cons: Some rooms are small with limited storage; no pool
Garden and pond mean the odd gecko or mosquito · the lane isn't an easy walk to the main temples — use the bikes

entries.name: Kantary Hotel Ayutthaya
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Rojana Road · city edge, near malls/markets
entries.storyHtml: Kantary is the Cape & Kantary 4-star where every room is a full-kitchen suite, scoring 9.2 from 176 reviews · Even the smallest Studio Suite is around 46 sqm, while the One and Two Bedroom suites are condo-sized, with a big fridge, microwave and dining nook · It's a strong pick for families and longer stays · The buffet breakfast is widely praised, and there's a pool, gym, sauna and free parking · It sits on the same Rojana Road as Classic Kameo.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Groups should go straight for a One or Two Bedroom Suite — better value than booking multiple rooms · The building has some age, so request a renovated or higher-floor room for a fresher feel.
pros: Condo-sized rooms; every one a full-kitchen suite with a big fridge
Varied buffet breakfast, widely praised
Pool, gym, sauna and free parking
Excellent value for families or longer stays
cons: City-edge Rojana Road location — can't walk to the ruins
The building and some rooms are showing their age

entries.name: Tamarind Guesthouse
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Chikun Road, Old Town island · across from Wat Mahathat
tags: 🛕 Walk across to the Buddha head in tree roots
entries.addr: 11 Moo 1, Chikun Road, Pratu Chai, Old Town island, Ayutthaya
entries.storyHtml: Tamarind Guesthouse has the best location in this guide — a 9.9 location score — because it sits directly across from Wat Mahathat; cross the road and in 2–3 minutes you're at the famous Buddha head in the tree roots · It's a restored old teak house tucked at the end of a quiet lane, with just 6 rooms decorated in silk and carved wood, en-suite bathrooms with rain showers · The owner speaks good English and is attentive, and the free breakfast includes homemade banana cake · Its 9.4 overall is very high for a budget stay.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Cross to Wat Mahathat at dawn before the crowds for quiet, beautiful shots of the Buddha head · With only 6 rooms, book weeks ahead and bring mosquito repellent.
pros: Right across from Wat Mahathat — walk the Old Town temples
Beautifully decorated teak rooms, clean, with rain showers
Owner speaks good English, attentive and helpful
Free freshly made breakfast with homemade banana cake
cons: Old wooden house — sound travels, mosquitoes in some seasons
No TV or lift, only 6 rooms — book well ahead

entries.name: iuDia Hotel
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Pratu Chai, Old Town island · riverside, by the historical park
entries.addr: 11-12 Moo 4, U-Thong Road, Pratu Chai, Old Town island, Ayutthaya
entries.storyHtml: iuDia Hotel is a tiny 13-room riverside boutique on the Old Town island, scoring 9.1 · What guests mention most is the riverside pool that looks across the Chao Phraya to the stupa of Wat Phutthaisawan, lit up at dusk · Rooms are larger than expected, warmly furnished, with private balconies · A past Thailand Boutique Award winner with attentive, personal service and free bikes for cycling to the temples · The charm is in the location and atmosphere — some rooms are due a refresh.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Specify a Riverview room for a balcony over the water · Take a swim at sunset and watch the temple opposite light up — the prettiest moment of the day.
pros: Riverside pool looking across to the temple's stupa
Riverside Old-Town location, walk to temples and the historical park
Spacious, warmly furnished rooms with private balconies
Friendly, attentive staff and free bicycles
cons: Some rooms show wear and are due a refresh
Only 13 rooms — fills fast · the pool is small and the wooden steps are slippery

entries.name: Baan Mee Suk Ayutthaya
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Maharat Road, Old Town island · 180 m to Wat Ratchaburana
entries.addr: 9, 12 Maharat Road, Pratu Chai, Old Town island, Ayutthaya
entries.storyHtml: Baan Mee Suk is the budget guesthouse with a genuinely temple-front location — about 180 m from Wat Ratchaburana and a few minutes from Wat Mahathat, with a 9.4 location score on Booking · What guests mention most is how clean and quiet the rooms are — parquet floors, soft beds, privacy curtains in the dorms · The husband-and-wife owners run it themselves, kind and welcoming, with free water, coffee and bread in the morning and bikes for rent · A 9.1 overall from 166 reviews, at backpacker prices.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: For privacy, choose a family room with an en-suite over the shared-bath Economy · Rent a bike and cycle the historical park in the early morning or evening when it's coolest.
pros: Excellent location — walk to Wat Ratchaburana and Wat Mahathat
Very clean rooms, calm and quiet
Kind husband-and-wife owners running it personally
Free water/coffee/bread and bikes for rent, great value
cons: Rooms are on the small side; the cheapest uses a shared bathroom
No hairdryer, no pool, occasional cigarette smell

entries.name: Busaba Ayutthaya
entries.mrtTag: 📍 U-Thong Road · riverside, north of the Old Town island
entries.addr: 56/2 Moo 3, U-Thong Road, Old Town island, Ayutthaya
entries.storyHtml: Busaba Ayutthaya is a concept hotel that gave a roughly 50-year-old Ayutthaya wooden house a new life, scoring 8.8 · It keeps the original frame and character while adding contemporary design, so many reviews say it feels like walking into an art piece · It sits on the river north of the Old Town island, with a riverside garden, a bar and fresh breakfast served by the water · It's about a 15-minute walk to Wat Mahathat, with free bikes · Note there's no pool, and some original rooms share a bathroom — pick an en-suite room.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Read the room details and pick a Deluxe with an en-suite bathroom if you want full privacy · Borrow a bike and visit the temples at dawn for quiet and good light.
pros: Distinctive design — a charming reworking of an old Ayutthaya house
Spotlessly clean; friendly, English-speaking staff
Quiet riverside garden, fresh breakfast served by the water
Good value, with free bikes
cons: No pool, and some rooms share a bathroom with the next room
Small property, few rooms, fills fast · quiet location, slightly off the main shopping area

entries.name: Krungsri River Hotel
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Rojana Road · Pa Sak riverside, 5 min walk to the train station
entries.storyHtml: Krungsri River Hotel is a 202-room 4-star on the Pa Sak river that sells location and convenience — about a 5-minute walk from Ayutthaya train station, scoring 8.4 from 232 reviews · It's an older business hotel whose main draw is the river view; the River View side looks down a long stretch of water with morning mist · There's a garden pool, spa, sauna and four restaurants, with a buffet breakfast that's often praised · A safe pick for train-arriving day-trippers who value location over a brand-new room.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: At booking, request a River View room on a higher floor — the difference is big · If you're a light sleeper, ask for a room away from the function rooms and restaurants, as some nights host events.
pros: Pa Sak riverside, walking distance to Ayutthaya train station
Lovely river-view rooms, especially on higher floors
Varied, often-praised buffet breakfast
Pool, spa, sauna and free parking
cons: Room decor is dated; some rooms are due a renovation
Fairly thin walls · staff service is formal rather than warm

adviceTitle: How to pick the right Ayutthaya stay for your trip?

advice.head: On a budget, want the best value
advice.bodyHtml: → Plus Hostel Ayutthaya ฿400 garden house with free dinner · or Baan Mee Suk ฿450, 180 m to Wat Ratchaburana · or Tamarind Guesthouse ฿650 across from Wat Mahathat

advice.head: Want to walk the Old Town temples
advice.bodyHtml: → Tamarind Guesthouse ฿650 across from Wat Mahathat · or Baan Mee Suk ฿450 walk to Wat Ratchaburana · or iuDia Hotel ฿2,500 riverside boutique by the park

advice.head: Special trip, want a riverside boutique
advice.bodyHtml: → SALA Ayutthaya ฿4,800 red brick on the Chao Phraya with stupa views, 9.3 · or iuDia Hotel ฿2,500 with a riverside pool facing a temple

advice.head: Family trip, self-driving
advice.bodyHtml: → Kantary Hotel ฿1,600 every room a full-kitchen suite · or Classic Kameo ฿1,700 spacious rooms with a kitchen and a pool, on Rojana Road

advice.head: Want a warm, homely feel
advice.bodyHtml: → Baan Tye Wang Guesthouse ฿1,200 Thai house in a garden, owner-run · or Plus Hostel ฿400 garden house with free home-cooked dinner

advice.head: Love distinctive design
advice.bodyHtml: → Busaba Ayutthaya ฿1,500 a 50-year-old Ayutthaya house reborn · or SALA Ayutthaya ฿4,800 red brick by Onion studio

advice.head: Arriving by train, want to walk in
advice.bodyHtml: → Krungsri River Hotel ฿1,800 a 5-minute walk from the train station, on the Pa Sak river · full-service with a pool and breakfast

noteHtml: 📌 Note: All prices are approximate and vary by date and season — always check live rates and compare 3 sites before booking · During long weekends and the cool season (November–February), prices rise and rooms fill fast, especially the riverside boutiques and small Old-Town guesthouses, so book ahead · Ayutthaya has no metro — arrive by train, minivan or car, and get around by bike or Grab · Guide by ThailandAddict.com
faqTitle: FAQ — Common traveller questions about Ayutthaya hotels

faq.q: ❓ Which area is best to stay in Ayutthaya?
faq.a: It depends on your style · The Old Town island is best if you want to walk or cycle to the temples (Tamarind, Baan Mee Suk, iuDia, Baan Tye Wang, Busaba, Plus Hostel) · The riverside is for quiet stays, some with stupa views (SALA Ayutthaya, Krungsri River) · Rojana Road suits self-drivers who want big rooms with a kitchen (Classic Kameo, Kantary) · If you don't have a car, the Old Town island is easiest for exploring on foot.

faq.q: ❓ How much do Ayutthaya hotels cost?
faq.a: Prices vary widely: budget hostels and guesthouses start around ฿350–650 a night · boutique guesthouses and 4-star Rojana Road hotels run ฿1,200–2,500 · upper-tier riverside boutiques start ฿2,500–4,800+ · During long weekends and the cool season, rates can run higher and rooms fill quickly.

faq.q: ❓ How far ahead should I book an Ayutthaya hotel?
faq.a: For ordinary weekdays, 1–2 weeks ahead is plenty · but during long weekends, the cool season (November–February) and festivals, the good places fill fast — especially riverside boutiques and small Old-Town guesthouses with only a handful of rooms — so book 3–4 weeks ahead or more.

faq.q: ❓ Which site is cheapest for booking Ayutthaya hotels?
faq.a: Prices on each site (Agoda, Booking.com, Trip.com) shift with each promotion, so open all three and compare before every booking — each review page in this guide includes price-comparison links, which can save hundreds of baht a night.

faq.q: ❓ Arriving in Ayutthaya by train — where should I stay?
faq.a: If you want to walk to your hotel from the station without a taxi · Krungsri River Hotel is about a 5-minute walk, a 4-star on the Pa Sak river · Old-Town stays like Tamarind or Baan Mee Suk require a short ride or ferry crossing, but you gain temple-walking convenience.

faq.q: ❓ Which Ayutthaya hotels are within walking distance of Wat Mahathat?
faq.a: Several Old-Town stays are walkable · Tamarind Guesthouse is directly across from Wat Mahathat, a 2–3 minute walk · Baan Mee Suk is 180 m from Wat Ratchaburana and minutes from Wat Mahathat · Early Bird and other central Old-Town stays are an easy walk or cycle away.
